newsitem.title: USA: Texaco says ahead of women, minority targets.
newsitem.headline: Texaco says ahead of women, minority targets.

text.p: Texaco chief executive Peter Bijur told the company's annual shareholder meeting that the company is ahead of its targets to recruit women and minorities.
Bijur said that 49 percent of new hires in the first quarter of 1997 were women and 36 percent from minorities
"During the first quarter the total number of women and minorities, including African Americans and Hispanics increased on an absolute basis an as a percentage of the workforce," Bijur said

Referring to a settlement reached in a class action by 1,400 employees last year, Bijur said the company had settled in order to avoid a protracted court fight, which could have resulted in a larger financial settlement than the $115 million the company paid ot plus an 11.4 percent pay rise for workers from minority groups.
Texaco offered to settle after tapes emerged in which company employees allegedly discused destroying documents and making racist remarks.
"The behaviour and tone of the tapes offended us all," Bijur said.
He said that Texaco was also increasing its business with women and minority owned firms and has financial agreements with 50 women and minority fimrs.
